To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

an increase in the plasma tryptophan/branched-chain amino acid ratio may induce fatigue during exercise by an increase in 3-5-HT synthesis in brain and that a decrease in plasma concentration of glutamine may induce an impairment of immune function by a decrease in synthesis of glutamine by skeletal muscle.
the metabolism of tryptophan and branched-chain (BCAAs) amino acids may be central to the etiology of central fatigue and the over-training syndrome.
the ratio of free trytophan to branched-chain amino acid in plasma is a key factor in central fatigue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of amino acids in the control of fatigue and immune function.
the role of specific nutrients in the etiology and prevention of fatigue in athletes, and in the etiology, prevention, and treatment of the overtraining syndrome.
elucidating the metabolic basis of fatigue, the overtraining syndrome, and immune dysfunction in athletes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
branched-chain amino acid metabolism is central to the etiology of central fatigue and overtraining syndrome and to the etiology, at least partially, of the overtraining syndrome.
the amino acid profile in blood and muscle is an important indicator of the nutritional status of the individual.
the metabolism of amino acids is important for the understanding of some aspects of the etiology of central fatigue, overtraining syndrome, and immunosuppression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amino acid profile of the plasma is a key factor in determining the balance between the anabolic and catabolic processes in the body and thus in determining health or illness.
the amino acid pool is an essential component of the metabolic link between the brain and skeletal muscle, the brain and the immune system, and between skeletal muscle and the immune system.
the metabolism of amino acids may be a key to understanding the pathogenesis of some aspects of fatigue, overtraining, and immune dysfunction in athletes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the amino acid metabolism in skeletal muscle and in the brain is tightly linked and that the metabolism of amino acids in skeletal muscle is a key factor in the control of the synthesis of 5-HT in the brain.

the metabolism of glutamate, glutamine, trytophan and branched chain amino acids may play important roles in the etiology, prevention, and treatment of fatigue and the immunosuppression of athletes and other individuals.

amino acid metabolism plays a key role in exercise-induced fatigue and in the overtraining syndrome and that the metabolism of branched-chain amino acid, tryptophane and glutamine may be the key in this regard.
